title: A resident's shelter on the summit, Núi Bà Đen
description: A woman in a pale blouse sits against a weathered boulder beside a lean-to of poles, sandbags and canvas, one arm along the rock; crates, a tin, a bucket and helmet liners lie under its bamboo frame, and a rolling field of sandbags fills the foreground. Beyond the scrub at left the mountain drops away into haze. "One of the residents. This is where she lived." Of the shelter: "Everything is made out of scrap. To get a stick like that you would go down into the jungle and carry it up." And of the people: "They were sick."
researchNotes: Identified by Larry on 2026-09-05 (giscus-vn-0039-c18308606.json), with the location given in his own words. This is the third of the summit domestic frames the survey grouped together, and the first that he has spoken to directly; 'they were sick' connects to the sick call he says he and the medic held for the strikers' families (VN-0041). His remark about sanitation is kept as given in the recollection record and not repeated here. The poles-and-scrap construction, and the effort of carrying timber up from the jungle, is the kind of texture the CIDG-camp histories never record.
